By Prop 3.9,

Π⁡(W,0)=−W3​(a23+a⁡(1−a)2​W+(1−a)25​W2).\Pi(W,0)=-W^{3}\bigl(\tfrac{a^{2}}{3}+\tfrac{a(1-a)}{2}W+\tfrac{(1-a)^{2}}{5}W^{2}\bigr).

One root is W=1W=1 by Thm 3.19, so the other is the ratio of constant to leading coefficient, namely 5​a2/(3​(1−a)2)5a^{2}/\bigl(3(1-a)^{2}\bigr). Using a2=−3​a−6a^{2}=-3a-6 one gets (1−a)2=−5​(a+1)(1-a)^{2}=-5(a+1), whence that root is (a+2)/(a+1)=(2−a)/4(a+2)/(a+1)=(2-a)/4.

Now β2=(2−a)2/16=(−7​a−2)/16\beta^{2}=(2-a)^{2}/16=(-7a-2)/16 and (1−a)​β=(−3​a−2)/2(1-a)\beta=(-3a-2)/2, so

φ⁡(β)=β2​(a+(1−a)​β)=−7​a−216⋅−a−22=−5​a−3832,\varphi(\beta)=\beta^{2}\bigl(a+(1-a)\beta\bigr)=\frac{-7a-2}{16}\cdot\frac{-a-2}{2}=\frac{-5a-38}{32},

and t=1/φ⁡(β)t=1/\varphi(\beta) is as stated; this is the first condition for φ~\widetilde{\varphi}. The second holds by Lem 3.10, since Π~​(1,0)=t2​β​Π​(β,0)=0\widetilde{\Pi}(1,0)=t^{2}\beta\,\Pi(\beta,0)=0. Finally, using (5​a+38)​(23−5​a)=1024(5a+38)(23-5a)=1024,

c~2=t​a​β2=2​a​(7​a+2)5​a+38=−1024​a−30721024=−3−a=a¯,\widetilde{c}_{2}=t\,a\beta^{2}=\frac{2a(7a+2)}{5a+38}=\frac{-1024a-3072}{1024}=-3-a=\bar{a},

and likewise c~3=t⁡(1−a)​β3=(43​a+122)/(5​a+38)=a+4=1−a¯\widetilde{c}_{3}=t(1-a)\beta^{3}=(43a+122)/(5a+38)=a+4=1-\bar{a}. ∎

Corollary 12.7.

The rescaling (t,β)(t,\beta) of Prop 12.6 is not induced by any element of 𝒢♯\mathcal{G}^{\sharp}. Consequently the two six-sheeted maps are distinct 𝒢♯\mathcal{G}^{\sharp}-orbits over ℚ¯\overline{\mathbb{Q}}, exchanged by Gal⁡(ℚ⁡(−15)/ℚ)\Gal(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-15})/\mathbb{Q}), the field of moduli of each equals its minimal field of definition,

FOM=FODmin=ℚ⁡(−15),\mathrm{FOM}=\mathrm{FOD}_{\min}=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-15}),

and Thm 12.2(3) is sharp as a moduli statement. The common unpointed quotient-cover class is defined over ℚ\mathbb{Q}, with seed φ0​(W)=W2+W3\varphi_{0}(W)=W^{2}+W^{3}, whose marking polynomial has the two admissible markings as roots of 6​W2+15​W+106W^{2}+15W+10; thus −15-15 is the discriminant of the marking cover of Thm 3.18 at (k,d)=(2,3)(k,d)=(2,3), not merely of a seed coefficient equation.

Proof.

The unpointed left–right self-equivalence group of the six-sheeted quotient cover is trivial. The line component is intrinsically distinguished by its semigroup ℤ≥0\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}. The non-line branch component has normalization 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1} with one place at infinity and two finite special points having distinct local value semigroups ⟨2,3⟩\langle 2,3\rangle and ⟨2,5⟩\langle 2,5\rangle. Any induced automorphism of that normalization fixes all three places and is therefore the identity. Thus the target automorphism fixes the non-line component pointwise; since that irreducible component is not a fence, the faithfulness theorem of Blanc–Stampfli [6] makes the target polynomial automorphism itself trivial. The remaining source automorphism is a deck transformation; the geometric monodromy is A6A_{6}, whose centralizer in its natural degree-six action is trivial. Hence the self-equivalence group is trivial. Hence the equivalence of Prop 12.6 is the unique unpointed equivalence between the two quotient classes. It carries the marking β\beta to the normalised marking and the distinguished point W=1W=1 to W=1/β≠1W=1/\beta\neq 1, so it is not a pointed equivalence, and none exists. By Thm 4.9, a 𝒢♯\mathcal{G}^{\sharp}-equivalence would induce a pointed equivalence of the rooted quotients; therefore the two maps are distinct 𝒢♯\mathcal{G}^{\sharp}-orbits, and the same argument applied over ℚ¯\overline{\mathbb{Q}} shows they are geometrically distinct. Complex conjugation interchanges aa and a¯\bar{a} and hence the two orbits, so Gal⁡(ℚ¯/ℚ)\Gal(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}) acts on the pair through Gal⁡(ℚ⁡(−15)/ℚ)\Gal(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-15})/\mathbb{Q}) with the nontrivial element acting nontrivially; the field of moduli of each orbit is therefore ℚ⁡(−15)\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-15}), and the model of Thm 3.19 realises it as a field of definition. For the last claim, the rescaling class of φ\varphi over ℚ¯\overline{\mathbb{Q}} contains φ0=W2+W3\varphi_{0}=W^{2}+W^{3}, whose marking polynomial is (6​W2+15​W+10)/30(6W^{2}+15W+10)/30 by direct integration, of discriminant class −15-15; normalising at either root recovers the two seeds by c2=1/(1+W)c_{2}=1/(1+W). ∎

13. Concluding remarks

We summarise what has been established. Every three-dimensional unit-positive weight (1,−r,−s)(1,-r,-s) carries a graded Keller counterexample (Cor 9.5); no assertion is made here for primitive hyperbolic weights outside this sector, such as (2,−1,−1)(2,-1,-1). The interior weights 2≤r≤s2\leq r\leq s come from the beta–Hermite construction, and the unit boundary from the cyclic, flagship, and propagated cubic constructions. Assuming Hypothesis 8.4, the flagship box has reduction equal to one orbit of the full degree-bound-preserving gauge group 𝒢=Blin×(𝔾m)3\mathcal{G}=B_{\mathrm{lin}}\times(\mathbb{G}_{m})^{3} and quotient the dual point. In the balanced signature, cyclic cones realise every composite generic fibre degree N≥6N\geq 6. At degree twelve the quartic seed curve gives infinitely many geometric graded orbits and a degree-six forgetful map to unpointed quotient classes, while the alternating shear lies in a separate left–right class. The local alternating-shear Keller locus is cut out unconditionally by Thm 11.1; its stable compactification and intersection class are the conditional conclusions of Theorems 11.5 and 11.6 under Hypothesis 11.3. The exact Nielsen-class computations and the cyclic lift-form arithmetic are as stated in Secs. 10 and 12.

Several structural questions remain, and the balanced ones are taken up in [15]. The first concerns fields of definition across the geography. The unit boundary r=1r=1 and the row r=2r=2 are rational, by the balanced 3333-sheeted witness Thm 3.20, the flagship normal form and propagated members Propositions 8.3 and 9.2, and Prop 4.5(1); for r≥3r\geq 3 the construction of Sec. 4 produces a member only over Kr=ℚ⁡(ζ)K_{r}=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta), which Prop 4.5(3) shows is totally imaginary whenever rr is odd. Whether those rows contain rational members, and whether a weight can force a nontrivial field of moduli as (1,−1,−1)(1,-1,-1) does at degree six, is open. Related is the minimal degree problem. For 𝐰=(1,−1,−2)\mathbf{w}=(1,-1,-2) it is settled by Thm 8.5: 𝐝=(4,3,1)\mathbf{d}=(4,3,1) is a coordinatewise minimal nonempty box, every lower stratum inside it being empty; Thm 8.5 does not exclude incomparable degree vectors. For 𝐰=(1,−1,−1)\mathbf{w}=(1,-1,-1) the differential obstruction of [15, Cor. 1.5] bounds the total degree of any member below by deg⁡A+deg⁡B+deg⁡Λ≥14\deg A+\deg B+\deg\Lambda\geq 14, while the smallest class realised here is 𝒴1,1,(8,14,1)∘\mathcal{Y}^{\circ}_{1,1,(8,14,1)} of total degree 2323, attained by the six-sheeted map of Thm 3.19. The frontier is the gap between the two, and with it the least generic fibre degree in the balanced signature, which Cor 3.7 leaves open below six.

The second group of questions concerns how the positive-dimensional seed loci from different factorizations N=k​dN=kd meet in a fixed bounded scheme. The general marking theorem gives dimension d−3d-3 inside each regular cyclic seed space, while Thm 7.9 determines the quartic component and its six-sheeted marking cover exactly. It remains to determine intersections and component structure among loci arising from different factorizations, and to compute the monodromy and arithmetic of the higher marking covers. The intrinsic invariants of the unpointed quotient cannot be complete, because a generic quartic quotient has six distinct graded lifts.

The infinitude in Thm 7.9 concerns geometric points. Over ℚ\mathbb{Q} it becomes the question whether E∘​(ℚ)E^{\circ}(\mathbb{Q}) is infinite, and that is open at both steps: no rational point of EE of projective height at most sixty exists, while EE has smooth points over ℝ\mathbb{R} and over ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p} for every p≤31p\leq 31. So it is undecided whether EE is an elliptic curve or a nontrivial torsor under its Jacobian, and the rank question comes only after that.

Every generic fibre degree realised at (1,−1,−1)(1,-1,-1) is composite: N=k​dN=kd with k≥2k\geq 2, d≥3d\geq 3 by Thm 3.11, and N=12N=12 in Secs. 5 and 7. Prime degree occurs at other weights, N=3N=3 at (1,−1,−2)(1,-1,-2) and at (1,−1,−s)(1,-1,-s). Whether a balanced member can have prime generic fibre degree is open.

The third direction is the Hurwitz-theoretic one. Which braid orbits of the Nielsen classes of Sec. 10.1 are realised by graded Keller maps is open wherever the class is not rigid; at p=3p=3 the question is empty by Prop 10.9. It has content for the alternating shear class, where by Prop 10.16 the Keller locus is a curve inside a fourfold. That curve is cut out exactly by Thm 11.1; assuming Hypothesis 11.3, its compactified class is determined by Thm 11.6; what remains is the full parabolic and logarithmic splitting of its normal bundle (Rem 11.7), the analogous compactified Keller loci in other Hurwitz components, and whether an unrealised point of ℋrd\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{rd}} is an obstruction imposed by the Keller condition or an artifact of the construction of Sec. 5.1; the same applies to the level-one Modular Tower question of Rem 10.15.

Finally, the arithmetic. The second lift condition at level kk is the vanishing of

𝒬n(k)​(φ)=∫0ϵφ​(W)kW2​𝑑W,\mathcal{Q}^{(k)}_{n}(\varphi)=\int_{0}^{\epsilon}\frac{\varphi(W)^{k}}{W^{2}}\,dW,

a form of degree kk in the seed coefficients reducing to the Hilbert form of Cor 12.1 at k=2k=2. Its isotropy over a given field, and a diagonalisation over ℚ\mathbb{Q} extending Thm 12.4 to all levels, are open. The coefficient field of the six-sheeted map of Thm 3.19 and that of F3,3F_{3,3} in Prop 4.5(2) both equal ℚ⁡(−15)\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-15}), the first from the discriminant of the binary moment form of Thm 12.2(3), the second from the quadratic factor of M3M_{3}, and we have no mechanism forcing the two to agree. By Lem 10.1 both covers have split-pair field ℚ⁡(5)\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5}) at infinity, while ℚ⁡(−3)\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) arises only from the unrelated (9,3)(9,3)-class of Thm 10.6, so ℚ⁡(−15)\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-15}) is the third quadratic subfield of ℚ⁡(5,−3)\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5},\sqrt{-3}).

Last, by Prop 3.21 a member of Sec. 3 descends to a two-variable Keller pair exactly when every monomial Λi​wj\Lambda^{i}w^{j} occurring in AA or BB satisfies i≥j−1i\geq j-1, and the obstruction is the single coefficient cd​Λ−dc_{d}\Lambda^{-d}. A construction of weight (1,−1,−1)(1,-1,-1) evading it would produce a noninjective planar Keller pair, contradicting the two-variable Jacobian Conjecture, so the substantive question is whether the failure is forced, and by what. This is the differential side of [15], where the balanced obstruction is developed in the form that yields the degree bound quoted above.
